messages.author: 3de7103b4d8a58a6
messages.subject: shiny-server startup errors
parts:
Hi,

I'm keen to get a site I'm developing with shiny up and running as a bona-fide standalone web-site.

To this end I've downloaded and installed the shiny-server[1] and because I use Gentoo Linux I am trying to write an init script based on the instructions for Ubuntu on the Wiki[2] and the sample init file for Ubuntu that is provided.

I'm following the Gentoo Handbook for writing Init scripts[3] and at present have...

#!/sbin/runscript
depend(){
  # Only start shiny-server after the network interface has been bought up
  after net
}
start(){
  ebegin "Starting shiny-server"
  start-stop-daemon --start --exec /usr/bin/shiny-server >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2
  local _retval=$?
  eend "${_retval}"
}
stop(){
  ebegin "Stopping shiny-server"
  start-stop-daemon --start --exec /usr/bin/shiny-server >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2  
  local _retval=$?
  eend "${_retval}"
}

(As a side question does the shiny-server when started generate a pid file, and if so whats the default location?).

When I run this I get the following error message...

/etc/init.d/shiny-server start
  * Starting shiny-server ...
  path.js:313
     throw new TypeError('Arguments to path.resolve must be strings');
                ^
   TypeError: Arguments to path.resolve must be strings
    at Object.exports.resolve (path.js:313:15)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/usr/lib64/node_modules/shiny-server/lib/main.js:52:25)
   at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
   at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
   at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
   at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
   at Function.Module.runMain (module.js:497:10)
   at startup (node.js:119:16)
   at node.js:901:3
   * start-stop-daemon: failed to start `/usr/bin/shiny-server'
   [ !! ]
   * ERROR: shiny-server failed to start


The log-file contains entries indicating that an attempt was made to start it...

[2013-05-10 14:08:29.801] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v0.3.5 (Node.js v0.10.5)

...
...but sure there is no server running (based on listing active processes) as I'd expect based on getting error messages.

I have as per the instructions created a user account ('shiny') for the server to run as and can start the server fine from the command line and have a simple directory listing of the root directory in /var/shiny-server/www/ (which is currently empty).

I'd really like to get this working as writing an init script for Gentoo is the starting point of writing an ebuild for others to install and use shiny-server on Gentoo.  Any help/pointers/suggestsions are gratefully received.

Thanks in advance for your time,

Neil

[1] https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/
[2] https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-server/wiki/Ubuntu-step-by-step-install-instructions
[3] http://www.gentoo.org/doc/en/handbook/handbook-x86.xml?part=2&chap=4#doc_chap4

messages.subject: Re: shiny-server startup errors
parts:
It looks like runscript is passing some arguments to shiny-server that the latter is not expecting. Can you try changing this:
>> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2

to this:

>> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1

shiny-server doesn't create a pid file, it also doesn't daemonize itself by forking though. Is that a problem for gentoo? If so do you have a link that explains how gentoo wants/expects these kind of processes to behave?

messages.author: 3de7103b4d8a58a6
messages.subject: Re: shiny-server startup errors
parts:
Hi Joe,

I've done some hunting around and asking in the Gentoo community.
On Friday, May 10, 2013 6:28:57 PM UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

shiny-server doesn't create a pid file, it also doesn't daemonize itself by forking though. Is that a problem for gentoo? If so do you have a link that explains how gentoo wants/expects these kind of processes to behave?

The pid file isn't a problem, its possible to have the init script create one on starting the process using a combination of the '--make-pidfile --pidfile "${PIDFILE}"' flags to the start-stop-daemon command.  Its also possible to daemonize the process using the '--background' flag of start-stop-daemon too.  So the init-script is now looking like...


#!/sbin/runscript

PIDFILE=/var/run/shiny-server.pid

depend(){

after net
}
start(){
   ebegin "Starting shiny-server"

start-stop-daemon --start --make-pidfile --pidfile "${PIDFILE}" \
    --background --exec /usr/bin/shiny-server >> /var/log/shiny-server.log 2>&1

local _retval=$?
    eend "${_retval}"
}
stop(){
   ebegin "Stopping shiny-server"
start-stop-daemon --stop --pidfile "${PIDFILE}"

local _retval=$?
   eend "${_retval}"
}

...and it appears to work fine with the examples.

Hope thats useful, I'll update/feedback when I make some progress on writing an ebuild to install shiny-server on Gentoo (a new learning curve for me though).

Neil
